conditions.advice: Rest, stay hydrated and use OTC symptom relief. See a doctor if symptoms last more than 10 days or worsen.
Rest in a quiet, dark room and consider an OTC analgesic. See a doctor if headaches are frequent, severe or sudden.
An antihistamine usually controls seasonal allergy symptoms. See a doctor if it interferes with daily life.
Rest, fluids and an antipyretic. Seek care if fever exceeds 39.5C or lasts more than 3 days.
Avoid trigger foods and consider an OTC antacid. See a doctor if it happens more than twice a week.
Stay hydrated with oral rehydration. See a doctor if there is blood, high fever or symptoms last more than 2 days.

red_flags.message: Chest pain can indicate a cardiac emergency.
Breathing difficulty requires immediate medical attention.
Shortness of breath requires immediate medical attention.
Symptoms involving blood require in-person evaluation.
Fainting or loss of consciousness requires immediate medical attention.
Sudden confusion requires immediate medical attention.
Self-reported severe symptoms require in-person evaluation.
A stiff neck with fever can indicate meningitis and needs urgent evaluation.
